target_customer: Mortgage lenders ordering residential appraisals, plus appraisal firms
problem: Residential appraisals take about a week and are slow and manual; AI plus LiDAR capture can compress report production.
business_model: AI-native appraisal firm charging per appraisal, with licensed appraisers reviewing and signing reports

founders.name: Humza Ahmed
education: University of Waterloo (dropped out, program listed as se)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page, family has worked in appraisal for about 40 years and the product began as internal tooling for a family appraisal business.

competitors.name: ValueMate
competitors.what: YC Spring 2025 startup using phone LiDAR to produce near-final appraisal reports and run its own appraisal firm

competitors.name: Aivre
competitors.what: AI appraisal workflow platform verified for UAD 3.6

competitors.name: Restb.ai
competitors.what: Computer vision tools for UAD 3.6 appraisals

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile LiDAR capture, computer vision and report-generating agents must meet GSE format rules; hard part is accuracy and compliance rather than new research.

defensibility.rationale: Licensed appraiser panel and GSE compliance add friction, but similar LiDAR approaches (ValueMate) and incumbents exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents launched UAD 3.6 tools in late 2025. A trade report says True Footage sued Automax in 2026 alleging it cloned software via fake MLS credentials, which Automax denies.

market_need_then: The UAD 3.6 appraisal form became mandatory for Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac conventional loans in 2026, and appraiser capacity is limited, increasing demand for automation.

branding.domain_note: Uses automax.ai; some directories write Automax AI or Automax.

identity.logo: Automax AI logo image, not described
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, direct, speed-focused, as in back in a day, not a week.

brand_strength.rationale: Name resembles car dealer and automation brands; no press about the brand itself found.

outcome_analysis: Automax.ai grew from the founder's family appraisal business and claims 3,000 reports a month, giving real domain insight. A 2025 seed with Pioneer Fund and YC followed. A 2026 lawsuit from True Footage is a legal risk, and competition from other AI appraisal tools is rising. Outcome is still open.
notes: Seed date and investors come from PitchBook and Preqin search snippets (both agree on 17 November 2025); amount undisclosed there. VCBacked and FundedIQ list 500K pre-seed December 2025 and one article says 500K seed; Fundz says 5M but links a Waterloo location, likely a different company. Amounts unverified, so amount is null. The lawsuit was seen in a pulse.bot summary and a National Mortgage News item, neither opened. Competitors are listed by 2025 sources found in search results.
